channel.title: User on KubeSphere
channel.description: Recent content in User on KubeSphere

item.title: Create a User
item.description: This section describes how to create a user. Prerequisites You need to have the User Management permission on the KubeSphere platform. For more information, refer to Users and Platform Roles. Steps Log in to the KubeSphere web console as a user with User Management permissions. Click Users and Roles Management. In the left navigation pane, select Users. On the page, click Create.

item.title: View User List
item.description: This section describes how to view the user list. Prerequisites You need to have the User View permission on the KubeSphere platform. For more information, refer to Users and Platform Roles. Steps Log in to the KubeSphere web console as a user with User View permissions. Click User and Role Management. In the left navigation pane, select Users. The user list provides the following information:

item.title: View User Details
item.description: This section introduces how to view user details. Prerequisites You need to have User Viewing permissions in the KubeSphere platform. For more information, please refer to Users and Platform Roles. Steps Log in to the KubeSphere web console as a user with User Viewing permissions. click Users and Role Management. In the left navigation pane, select Users. In the user list, click the name of a user to open their details page.

item.title: Edit User Information
item.description: This section describes how to edit user information. You can edit a user’s alias, email, platform role, and description. KubeSphere does not support editing the username of a created user. Prerequisites You need to have the User Management permission on the KubeSphere platform. For more information, see Users and Platform Roles. Steps Log in to the KubeSphere web console as a user with User Management permissions.

item.title: Edit Current User Information
item.description: This section describes how to modify the current user’s email information and the interface display language. Prerequisites You have obtained the username and password for the KubeSphere web console. Steps Log in to the KubeSphere web console. In the upper-right corner of the page, click the current username, then select User Settings from the dropdown list. On the Basic Information tab, set the user’s email and language.

item.title: Change User Password
item.description: This section describes how to change a user password. Change the Current User’s Password Log in to the KubeSphere web console. In the upper-right corner of the page, click the current username, and then select User Settings from the drop-down list. Click the Password Settings tab to change the password of the current user. The password must contain at least one digit, one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, and one special character (~!

item.title: Reset User Password
item.description: This section describes how to reset a user password. If a regular user forgets their password and cannot log in to the KubeSphere web console, please refer to this document to have an administrator change the user’s password. If a platform administrator forgets their password, execute the following command on the host cluster to modify the password for the specified account. kubectl patch users <USERNAME> -p '{"spec":{"password":"<YOURPASSWORD>"}}' --type='merge' && kubectl annotate users <USERNAME> iam.

item.title: Set Password Expiration
item.description: This section describes how to set password expiration to enforce periodic password changes and provide reminders before passwords expire. Prerequisites You need to be a member of a cluster and have the cluster-admin role within that cluster. Steps Log in to the KubeSphere web console as a user with the cluster-admin role and enter your cluster. Click Configuration > Secret in the left navigation pane.

item.title: Enable and Disable Two-Factor Authentication
item.description: This section describes how to enable and disable two-factor authentication for the current user. After enabling two-factor authentication, when a user logs in, they must enter a dynamic verification code generated by an authenticator app after providing their username and password. With two-factor authentication, users add an extra layer of security to their account using both a password and their mobile device. Prerequisites You have obtained the username and password for the KubeSphere web console.

item.title: Enable and Disable Users
item.description: This section describes how to enable and disable users. A disabled user cannot log in to the KubeSphere web console. Prerequisites You need to have the User Management permission on the KubeSphere platform. For more information, please refer to Users and Platform Roles. Enable and Disable a Single User Log in to the KubeSphere web console as a user with User Management permissions.

item.title: Delete Users
item.description: This section describes how to delete users. Prerequisites You need to have the User Management permission on the KubeSphere platform. For more information, see Users and Platform Roles. Delete a Single User Log in to the KubeSphere web console as a user with User Management permissions. Click User and Role Management. Select Users from the left navigation pane. Click on the right side of the user you want to delete, and then select Delete from the dropdown list.
